messages.label: navigate to /oauth/authorize
messages.note: a fresh state is generated and kept in sessionStorage

messages.label: GET /oauth/authorize ?response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state
messages.note: client_id and redirect_uri are checked first — 400 here, never a redirect

messages.label: 302 → auth-front /login?interaction=<id>
messages.note: no session cookie for this client yet

messages.label: GET /oauth/interactions/:id
messages.note: public — the login page holds no credential of any kind

messages.label: POST /oauth/login · { clientId, email, password }
messages.note: the same 401 for an unknown email and for a wrong password

messages.label: 204 · Set-Cookie oauth_session
messages.note: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, 30 days — bound to this one client

messages.label: POST /oauth/interactions/:id/accept · credentials: include
messages.note: no credentials — the session cookie names who accepts

messages.label: 200 { redirectTo }
messages.note: the code is issued here and the request is deleted

messages.label: GET /callback?code&state
messages.note: state is compared with the stored one and discarded in the same step

messages.label: POST /oauth/token · grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, client_id
messages.note: no client_secret — a public client has none to send

messages.label: 200 { access_token, refresh_token, expires_in, scope }
messages.note: the code is spent before any of its checks run

messages.label: GET /oauth/jwks
messages.note: indicated, not used: this client verifies with a bundled public.pem copy

messages.label: 200 { keys: [{ kid, n, e, alg: RS256 }] }
session stored · signed in
messages.note: RS256 verified with Web Crypto, then iss and client_id read from the claims

cards.title: Through the browser
items: state is the whole of this client's front-channel protection — no PKCE
The code travels in the address bar, so it is single-use and short-lived
auth-front only ever learns an interaction id, never where the code goes

cards.title: What the provider owns
items: Accounts belong to one client: the same email under two clients is two people
The session cookie shortcuts that one client only — this is not SSO
The password reaches POST /oauth/login and nothing else

cards.title: Single use
items: Issuing the code claims the authorization request and deletes it
The code is consumed first, then validated — a replay revokes the tokens it produced
A second callback fails on state, which was taken and cleared at once
